q: To generate code that is not merely correct but genuinely organic, we introduce Learning to Commit, a framework centred on Online Repository Memory.
r: EC6: new repository-memory technique evaluated on SWE-bench-style issue resolution, which is always excluded.

q: We formulate task-conditioned tool-output pruning as a benchmark task for coding agents
r: EC6: tool-output pruning model and dataset, not code development or evaluation of agents building applications.

q: We compared ways to fill a coding agent’s context budget at equal per-issue budgets on 300 testgraded issues with two model families.
r: EC6: context-compression comparison on SWE-bench issue repair, always excluded.

q: the first open-source benchmark for assessing autonomous software engineering through specification-driven, from-scratch system construction in MoonBit
r: Include: new benchmark evaluating coding agents (Codex CLI, Claude Code, etc.) building projects from specifications.

q: We define a benchmark structure spanning requirement-style incremental development, specification-driven development, and bug fixing.
r: Include: app-level benchmark for coding agents with feature-level tasks, run-to-run variation and resource use reported.

q: ProjectEval fills the gap in existing benchmarks by offering a user-focused framework with real-world applicability with comprehensive and project-level metrics.
r: Include: new project-level benchmark and evaluation method for code-generation agents building applications from requirements.

q: we introduce WebGen-Bench, a novel benchmark designed to measure an LLM-based agent’s ability to create multi-file website codebases from scratch.
r: Include: new benchmark comparing code-agent frameworks building web applications from instructions.

q: This paper proposes a new benchmark, Web-Bench, which contains 50 projects, each consisting of 20 tasks with sequential dependencies.
r: Include: new project-level benchmark with sequential feature tasks for LLM and agent evaluation.

q: we conduct the first controlled user study to understand how developers interact with coding agents and compare them to existing copilots.
r: Include: controlled within-participant comparison of coding agent vs copilot with human-effort and productivity measures.

q: We introduce Doc2Feat-Bench, a challenging benchmark for evaluating software engineering capabilities in documentation-driven feature addition.
r: Include: new benchmark of feature-addition tasks from documentation, evaluating agent scaffolds (OpenHands) with token consumption.
